summary: Added one behavior-only table regression to preserve the observed global-feedback-compatible registration flow without freezing feedback text/style/policy. The new focused test passed all three isolated held-provider branches: known transport failure, unknown outcome, and pending-registration success; current login form remained present/enabled, transaction classifications remained distinct, no automatic/safe retry was available for failures, and no additional registration call occurred. The entire controller suite and bounded public-site renderer suite also passed. Passwords were generated at runtime and absent from controller/runtime/Parts/storage/rendered tree. This is compatibility coverage, not a defect fix or browser acceptance claim.

source.head: b9eff6a0c4385ed2648e97b30d15366910b7b58b
source.git_changes: only the one intended test-file edit

test.name: held registration completion on login preserves transaction classification without replay
common_observations: Each branch held the actual Registration.registerTeacher fixture call, then navigated to /login before release.
At completion the current route/rendered page stayed login and the actual login form/submit control remained present/enabled.
After completion snapshot, invalid login reached existing validation_failed locally and added no registration call.
Generated password was absent from controller state, runtime snapshot, runtime inspection, actual PxC Part values, storage and rendered tree before and after local login validation.
test.phase_qualification: Completion statuses above were captured before the separate invalid-login control. Subsequent login validation changed controller request/outcome projection; those later values are not reported as registration completion state.

commands.command: node --test --test-concurrency=2 --test-name-pattern='held registration completion on login preserves transaction classification without replay' checkpoint/vendor/hh/src/public-controller.test.mjs

limits: Compatibility regression only; no controller/source policy change, defect correction, or red-before-fix claim.
Local fixture/controller/render-tree only; no real provider/backend, browser, production authority, Python runtime, or network operation.
No global feedback message/style/visibility policy is asserted.
No canonical build, independent review, commit, push, or publication was part of E1603.
